analysis: The method getDisplayElement() first checks if this.display is null. If null, it evaluates Configuration.errorOnAutoCreate(). If true, it throws a new Error with the message 'Attempt to auto-create Coding.display'. This is a defensive check that immediately fails when the configuration prohibits auto-creation and the display is absent. The use of Error (instead of a checked exception or a more specific RuntimeException) indicates that the programmer considers this situation a serious, unrecoverable fault—likely a configuration mistake or a programming error where the caller failed to ensure the display is set. The throw is unconditional once errorOnAutoCreate is true; there is no try-catch within the method, so the Error propagates upward. The programmer’s intent is to force an abrupt termination or at least a very visible failure, not to provide a recoverable condition. Therefore, the programmer did not expect or intend for the caller to catch this Error; it is meant to be an uncaught runtime error that signals a fatal problem.
